REQ-023 (waitlist auto-promotion on a freed seat, halting at T-24h, GitHub issue #26, fifth requirement of Phase 4) had RELEASE-VALIDATOR PASS at Step 5 (commit 755468d, 'chore(WF02-REQ-023): RELEASE-VALIDATOR gate -- PASS (Step 5)'). Verified the factual claims directly against the real code before writing the status-history note, rather than trusting the task prompt's summary: read apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts's isAutoPromotionHalted (lines 744-746, `startsAt.getTime() - evaluationTime.getTime() <= AUTO_PROMOTION_HALT_WINDOW_MS`, inclusive at exactly T-24h) and apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's decidePromotionEligibility (lines 330-344, pure first-match-wins: event-not-eligible -> halted-t24h -> capacity-full -> ok) and promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible (lines 361 onward), confirming it reuses REQ-020's exact `tx.select(...).from(events)...for("update")` lock discipline inside the SAME transaction handle withdrawRegistration() is already inside (never opens its own db.transaction), and selects the rank-1 waitlisted candidate by the same (created_at, id) tie-break REQ-021's getWaitlistPosition() established. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md section 5 in full and confirmed the at-most-once notification guarantee is genuinely state-derived: no new column exists anywhere (git-grep-level confirmation carried over from RELEASE-VALIDATOR's own re-verification), the guard is the promoted row's own admission='admitted' transition making it permanently unselectable by the waitlisted-row filter, so a second invocation against the same freed seat finds seatsLeft<=0 and refuses before ever reaching candidate selection -- takes no action, sends nothing, not because a marker suppressed a duplicate. Read apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts and confirmed sendPromotionNotification() is called only after withdrawRegistration()'s transaction has already committed (a separate, later step, not part of the same transaction) and that the S10 blocked-user skip (domain/user.ts's getUserForNotificationById() blocked projection + withdraw.ts's blocked check) was a real gap found and fixed at this run's Step 2c, with ISS-0020 correctly filed (MAJOR, out of scope) for the same pre-existing gap in REQ-018's staff.ts. Confirmed no schema change (git diff master...HEAD --stat shows no new drizzle migration file).

Content correction made to docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-023 entry (beyond the status flip): its description's notification-guarantee clause originally read 'this requirement guarantees at-most-once by making the promotion write and the send-marker part of the same transaction' -- this is factually wrong for the shipped mechanism (there is no send-marker of any kind, and the notification send happens strictly after, not inside, the promotion transaction). Reworded to describe the real state-derived guard (the admission='admitted' transition itself) and its real, narrower scope boundary (a crash between commit and the actual Telegram send is a genuine, still-open at-least-once-delivery gap explicitly left for REQ-025's future persistent ledger to close) -- matching docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md section 5 exactly.
